passage: Darshan had knocked the clay water pot off the ledge while chasing the calf, and it broke into six pieces. He scooped them up and pushed them under the straw in the cowshed. At dinner Ma searched the corner where the pot always stood. "Has anyone seen it?" Darshan pushed his roti away. His elder brother Madhav glanced at him but said nothing. All night the secret sat on his chest like a stone. In the morning he found his parents on the veranda. "Ma, Papa, I broke the pot. I hid it in the cowshed. I'm sorry." Ma sighed. "I'd rather you told me at once. Come, we'll buy another on Thursday." Darshan breathed out, long and slow.

qa.q: Where did Darshan hide the pieces of the pot?
qa.a: He pushed them under the straw in the cowshed.

qa.q: What was Darshan feeling when he pushed his roti away at dinner?
qa.a: He felt worried and guilty. The secret sat on his chest like a stone, so he could not eat.

qa.q: What did confessing change, and what could Darshan do next time?
qa.a: It lifted the weight and showed his parents he could be trusted. Next time he could tell them right after the accident.

qa.q: How might Ma have felt when Darshan told her the truth?
qa.a: She was probably sad about the pot but glad he came forward. She did not scold him and even planned to buy another.

grounding: Shows a child who hid broken pieces, felt the secret grow heavy, and found relief in telling the truth late.
